news.title: Southern California Port Employers Say No Movement on Watchmen Contract Talks as Strike Risk Grows
news.summary: Negotiations between port employers and roughly 250 ILWU Local 26 watchmen at Los Angeles and Long Beach have stalled ahead of a Nov. 21 contract expiry, and the union has already authorized a strike.
news.why: Importers with boxes landing at San Pedro Bay late this month should line up contingency drayage, consider routing urgent freight via other gateways and watch for picket-line terminal closures.

news.title: BNSF Files Detailed Opposition to UP-NS Merger
news.summary: BNSF submitted a formal objection to the Surface Transportation Board arguing the Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern combination rests on flawed traffic forecasts and would shield less than 1% of rail volume with its pricing protections.
news.why: Shippers relying on rail or intermodal should weigh in during the STB review now, because a transcontinental merger could reshape routing options and pricing leverage for years.

news.title: Malaysia Loosens Rare Earths Curbs for France
news.summary: Following a visit by President Macron, Malaysia agreed to allow some unprocessed rare-earth exports to France to feed a joint separation venture due to start up next year.
news.why: Manufacturers dependent on magnets and critical minerals gain another non-Chinese supply pathway to watch, which could ease concentration risk in 2027 sourcing plans.

news.title: Survey: U.S. Trucking Operators Expect Fleets to Grow Over Next Year
news.summary: A Bain & Company poll of 210 American fleet operators shows close to four in five plan to add trucks over the coming year, with fuel costs ranked as the biggest operating headache.
news.why: Expanding carrier capacity could temper truckload rate increases in 2027, giving shippers room to negotiate contracts—though high diesel prices will keep surcharges elevated.

news.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum Celebrates Development of Interoceanic Corridor
news.summary: Speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Mexico's president pitched the Isthmus of Tehuantepec rail corridor as an emerging option to the Panama Canal, backed by large public and private infrastructure spending.
news.why: Importers moving goods between Asia and the U.S. East or Gulf coasts may eventually get a land-bridge alternative worth benchmarking against canal and all-water services.

news.title: Transportation Secretary Duffy Says U.S. Taking Steps to Avoid Future Aviation Disruptions
news.summary: After a faulty network router caused a nationwide ground stop of nearly five hours on Nov. 13, the FAA halted further installs pending lab tests and the DOT asked Congress for $50 billion more for air traffic modernization.
news.why: Air cargo users should build buffer time into peak-season time-critical shipments, since ATC system fragility can ground freight with no warning.

news.title: Amazon to expand fuel and logistics surcharge to more services
news.summary: Starting in February, Amazon will apply a 3.5% fuel-and-logistics surcharge to transport fees for its bulk storage and replenishment services, pointing to higher fuel costs.
news.why: Sellers using Amazon's upstream warehousing should rebuild 2027 landed-cost models to include the new fee and compare it against third-party prep and storage options.

news.title: Wrangler parent company plans to beef up inventory spending
news.summary: Kontoor Brands is committing about $50 million to rebuild stock after a weak third quarter in which its inventory dropped 6% from a year earlier.
news.why: Apparel suppliers and mills could see stronger orders from Kontoor in coming months, while competing brands should check whether lean stock positions are costing them sales.

news.title: How to prepare for the most severe El Niño on record
news.summary: Specialists are urging manufacturers to stress-test equipment and facilities for weather-driven failures as an exceptionally strong El Niño develops.
news.why: Buyers sourcing crops, hydropower-dependent goods or freight through weather-sensitive lanes like Panama should map exposure now and secure alternates before disruptions hit.

news.title: US Foods to test inventory-scanning robots at 6 more warehouses
news.summary: The foodservice distributor intends to launch inventory-scanning robot pilots at six additional facilities before year-end, its CEO told investors.
news.why: Distributors adopting automated cycle counting can raise inventory accuracy, a sign that customers may soon expect tighter fill rates and fewer substitutions.

news.title: Gulf Oil Flow at Risk From Lack of Empty Tankers, Tracker Says
news.summary: Tanker-tracking data show fewer empty vessels heading to load Middle East crude, which could undercut the recent rebound in Gulf oil exports.
news.why: A renewed squeeze on Gulf crude would feed straight into diesel and bunker costs, so freight buyers should expect fuel surcharges to stay volatile.

news.title: Second Strike on LPG Tanker in Strait of Hormuz Leaves One Missing, Two Injured
news.summary: The Panama-flagged gas carrier TARA GAS was hit again in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and two hospitalized.
news.why: Continued attacks keep war-risk premiums and energy prices high, so importers should budget for elevated ocean and fuel-linked costs on Middle East-exposed lanes.

news.title: LPG Tanker Reported to Have Sunk Off Bulgaria's Black Sea Coast
news.summary: Bulgaria's defense ministry says an LPG tanker went down off its coast, not far from where another vessel sank after a drone strike a day earlier.
news.why: Shippers with Black Sea cargo—grain, fertilizer, steel—should expect higher insurance costs and possible carrier reluctance to call in the region.

news.title: MIT Report: Corporate commitment to sustainability soars, but roadblocks to execution remain
news.summary: MIT's 2026 survey of over 1,800 supply chain professionals finds most firms value sustainability more than before, yet about 70% say tariff turbulence has delayed or shrunk their green initiatives.
news.why: Procurement teams should expect customers to keep asking for emissions data even as budgets tighten, so low-cost supplier data collection is a smart hedge.
